role_agent_name: Industrial hygiene and gas safety manager (HYG)
abstract: Maintains chemical neutralization flux, scrubber bypass configurations, and toxic gas residence metrics
system_message:
You are Industrial hygiene and gas safety manager (HYG). The industrial hygiene and gas safety manager maintains data on chemical neutralization flux, scrubber bypass configurations, toxic gas residence metrics, and gas detector calibration schedules.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains chemical neutralization flux, scrubber bypass configurations, and toxic gas residence metrics（TOX）
information_points.content:
HYG-TOX-7VK：For the Multi-Stage Reactive Bed Adsorption Protocol, the emergency bypass system activation is confirmed to be true for the specialty gas exhaust trunk line, the exhaust contact duct residence time between the reaction chamber and tertiary filter intake is 1.8 s under peak emergency exhaust draw, and the effective chemical adsorption flux is 35 kg/m2 across standardized arsine and silane vapor streams.
HYG-TOX-N2V：For the Vapor-Phase Chemo-Catalytic Neutralization Protocol, the emergency bypass system activation is confirmed to be true for the specialty gas exhaust trunk line, the exhaust contact duct residence time across the reaction chamber to tertiary filter intake is 1.2 s under peak emergency exhaust draw, and the effective chemical adsorption flux measures 15 kg/m2 prior to media saturation.
HYG-TOX-ET7：For the Sub-Atmospheric Cryogenic Scrubbing Protocol, the emergency bypass system activation is confirmed to be true based on automated actuator readiness on the specialty gas exhaust trunk line, the exhaust contact duct residence time from the reaction chamber to the tertiary filter intake is 3.0 s under peak emergency exhaust draw, and the effective chemical adsorption flux is 25 kg/m2 for a standardized arsine and silane vapor stream prior to saturation.

information_points.title: Detector calibration（CALIB）
information_points.content:
HYG-CALIB-3JP：For the Sub-Atmospheric Cryogenic Scrubbing Protocol, the hydride sensor calibration interval for electrochemical arsine and phosphine sensor heads is 60 d between bump tests and span calibrations.
HYG-CALIB-REI：For the Multi-Stage Reactive Bed Adsorption Protocol, the hydride sensor calibration interval for electrochemical arsine and phosphine sensor heads is 90 d between bump tests and span calibrations.
HYG-CALIB-52B：For the Vapor-Phase Chemo-Catalytic Neutralization Protocol, the hydride sensor calibration interval for electrochemical arsine and phosphine sensor heads is 30 d between bump tests and span calibrations.
